newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan official to visit Peru, Cuba and Dominica.
newsitem.headline: Japan official to visit Peru, Cuba and Dominica.

text.p: A top Japanese foreign ministry official will visit Peru, Cuba and the Dominican Republic next week to discuss the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, a government spokesman announced on Friday.
Vice foreign minister Masahiko Komura will leave Tokyo on Monday for a one-week visit to the three countries, chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters.
Komura will meet Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to urge a peaceful resolution of the 12-week crisis, and visit Cuba and the Dominican Republic to get their views on the issue, Kajiyama said.

Government sources said Komura's visits to Cuba and the Dominican Republic were to seek their cooperation in the event the rebels holding the hostages agree to go into exile in a country outside Peru.
Mediators met on Thursday with the leader of the Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima to explore ways of ending the standoff.
But the mediators, members of a three-man guarantors commission, gave no sign of any progress in the talks and did not say when the next round of talks might be.
